speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. You also mentioned a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. To help me understand what is happening, have you noticed any redness or warmth in the affected areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome)

The history of a painful, swollen left ankle followed by right knee inflammation, urinary pain, and a sexual history strongly suggests Reactive Arthritis. Given the age and symptoms, I will also need to rule out gonococcal arthritis with a Joint_Aspiration and Urine_Culture.
